title: Euclidean quotient
description: Write a = b*q + r with the remainder r satisfying 0 <= r < |b| (never negative, whatever the signs of a and b); return the quotient q. For example a = -7, b = 2 gives q = -4 (r = 1), a = 7, b = -2 gives q = -3 (r = 1), and a = -7, b = -2 gives q = 4 (r = 1). b is never 0 and may be negative.
notes: Experiment int_division: hidden tests use negative operands; the description states Euclidean-style non-negative remainder in words. The ref.zehn is written with int.div_floor / int.div_trunc / int.rem_euclid so it is valid under int_ops=operators and int_ops=explicit.
